headline: Bangladesh lose first T20I to Zimbabwe by 32 runs
summary: Despite a half-century from Yasir Ali, Bangladesh was bowled out for 138 while chasing 171, starting the series with a defeat.
details: Bangladesh lost the first T20I of a three-match series against Zimbabwe in Bulawayo, falling 32 runs short of the target of 171 runs.
Chasing the target, Bangladesh's top order collapsed, losing three wickets for just 34 runs, including Saif Hassan, Tanjid Hasan, and Parvez Hossain.
Yasir Ali provided a fighting effort, scoring 54 runs off 38 balls after returning to T20Is after three years, but his dismissal ended Bangladesh's hopes.

caption:
A fighting half-century from Yasir Ali wasn't enough as Bangladesh loses the first T20I to Zimbabwe by 32 runs.

Bangladesh lost the first T20I of a three-match series against Zimbabwe in Bulawayo, falling 32 runs short of the target of 171 runs.

Chasing the target, Bangladesh's top order collapsed, losing three wickets for just 34 runs, including Saif Hassan, Tanjid Hasan, and Parvez Hossain.

Yasir Ali provided a fighting effort, scoring 54 runs off 38 balls after returning to T20Is after three years, but his dismissal ended Bangladesh's hopes.

Tawhid Hridoy and Yasir Ali added 39 runs for the fourth wicket, while Yasir and Mehidi Hasan Miraz added 52 runs for the sixth wicket.

Bangladesh was eventually bowled out for 138 runs, losing their final five wickets for just 8 runs.

Earlier, Nahid Rana stood out for Bangladesh, taking 4 wickets for 26 runs in 4 overs, though he conceded 18 runs in his final over.

Zimbabwe scored 170 for 6, with Brian Bennett scoring 44 off 30 balls and late contributions from Ryan Burl and Evans

The second T20I of the series will take place in Bulawayo on July 17.

headline_marked: 2 more die as [[dengue deaths rise to 30]] in Bangladesh
headline: 2 more die as dengue deaths rise to 30 in Bangladesh
summary: At least 329 patients were hospitalised in 24 hours, with both recent deaths reported from Dhaka South City Corporation areas.
details: According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), at least two dengue patients died and 329 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00 am today.
Both of the reported deaths occurred in the Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) areas.
With these latest figures, the total number of dengue deaths in the country has risen to 30, while the total number of cases has reached 9,370.
The DGHS data further reveals that 880 dengue patients are currently undergoing treatment at various hospitals across the country.
caption:
Dengue deaths in Bangladesh have reached 30, with 2 more people dying in just 24 hours.

According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), at least two dengue patients died and 329 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00 am today.

Both of the reported deaths occurred in the Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) areas.

With these latest figures, the total number of dengue deaths in the country has risen to 30, while the total number of cases has reached 9,370.

The DGHS data further reveals that 880 dengue patients are currently undergoing treatment at various hospitals across the country.
